name: mapping_nul_byte_round_trips_in_string
description: put stores a string with an embedded NUL byte (\u0000 mid-string). The wire and the C ABI never carry a literal NUL inside a C string for this: JSON escaping represents it as the 6-byte sequence \u0000, so bc_put/bc_get's `char *json_data` parameters are always NUL-terminated at the end of the JSON text, never truncated early by the embedded byte. Verified directly against the daemon: a put-then-get round trip returns the full string unmodified. Every binding whose native string type is 8-bit-clean (not itself NUL-terminated) must decode the full value. The C SDK ships no JSON code of its own (sdks/c/runner_json.h docblock) -- conformance_runner.c's own throwaway JSON parser stores strings as C char* and its equality checks are length-aware (str_len-tracked, memcmp-based) specifically so this fixture proves something rather than accidentally passing via truncated strcmp.
